summary: A deployed default Flask histogram turned request-controlled raw paths into unbounded labels: at every checkpoint Flask series equaled 17 times the method/path/status tuple count plus 13, and 2,476 new tuples produced exactly all 42,092 new Flask series. Confirmed automated-style 404 probing triggered expensive multiprocess collection and serialization, and Kubernetes OOM-killed the sole relay.
impact: Production was intermittently unavailable during an approximately 87-minute crash loop, and repeated termination created an unquantified risk of losing active memory-backed relay state; no customer data loss was proven.
fix: The bounded-metrics backport is deployed in production Helm revision 7 as the identity-verified sha-6c39adc artifact. Authenticated application scraping was restored with 227 bounded samples and no raw canary or pid-label occurrences; the final six-minute soak had zero restarts, OOM recurrence, HTTP 429, or HTTP 5xx. Operationally resolved at 2026-09-05T19:53:19Z; the canonical preventive action items remain open.
lessons: The exact 17-times series fingerprint and low-reuse 404 aggregates confirmed both the cardinality defect and automated-style trigger without actor attribution. Release parity and negative-test coverage must prevent divergent artifacts from omitting existing hardening; pod-lifetime multiprocess state needs safe startup cleanup, and one replica amplified the outcome.
